body.p: Status of the Claims
The Office Action addresses and rejects claims 1-18. Reconsideration is respectfully requested.
Claims 2-3, 6, 11-12, and 15 are canceled without prejudice or disclaimer.

Claims 1, 7, 10, and 16 are amended as indicated above. Support for these amendments can be found throughout the specification and drawings, for example, at least in original claims 2-3, 6, 11-12, and 15 and in FIGS. 7 and paragraphs [0008]-[0009], [0011]-[0012], [0029], [0032]-[0033], [0038], [0040], [0051], [0056]-[0057] of the published application. No new matter is added.
The Office Action rejects claims 1-18 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being directed to a judicial exception without significantly more. Office Action, pp. 2-4.
Applicants respectfully disagree. However, solely in order to advance prosecution, claim 1 is amended to recite, in part,
a server configured to:
receive the user information from one or more of the portable device and
the vehicle terminal and determine whether the received user information is
recognizable; and
determine whether to store the user information as a new data set based on
the number of times the user information is received in response to determining that
the user information is unrecognizable;
wherein the user information includes vehicle setting values and attribute
information linked to the vehicle setting values;
wherein the attribute information includes vehicle setting functions and key
IDs respectively matched to the vehicle setting functions; and
wherein the server informs the one or more of the portable device and the
vehicle terminal that the new data set is stored when the user information is stored
as the new data set."
Aa discussed in detail below, submit that the claim 1 recites patent eligible subject matter.

Pursuant to M.P.E.P. § 2106(d)(1), a claim reciting a judicial exception is not directed to the judicial exception if it also recites additional elements demonstrating that the claim as a whole integrates the exception into a practical application. For example, the claimed subject matter may integrate the judicial exception into a practical application by demonstrating that it improves the relevant existing technology.

As discussed in paragraph [0003] of the published application, a connected service can provide a more comfortable and smart environment to a vehicle user by operating a connected vehicle using a portable device. For example, a connected service can transmit, for each user, setting input information input to the portable device to a server. The server can backup the setting information and download the backed up setting information to a vehicle. This allows the user to use a setting function input on the portable device (e.g., a vehicle window opening/closing control, screen brightness control, etc.) merely by boarding the vehicle.

As further discussed in paragraph [0004] of the published application, in a connected vehicle of a newer vehicle model, attributes of a setting function compared to a setting function previously stored in the server can be changed. As a result, a version of the server must be updated with a data set that includes attributes of the setting function of an existing vehicle model and the new model. It is an inconvenience to require update of the server to use the connected service each time a new vehicle model is released. Furthermore, it can be difficult to use the connected service when an error occurs in an update process.

The pending claims recite limitations that solve this problem. For example, claim 1 recites a server configuered to determine that user information is unrecognizable, determine whether to store user information that is determined to be unrecognizable as a new data set based upon a number of times the unrecognizable user information is received, and inform one or more of a portable device or a vehicle terminal that the new data set is stored when storing the unrecognized user information as a new data set. As discussed in paragraph [0065] of the instant application, these features reduce

the above-referenced inconvenience in a connected vehicle because the data set including the attributes of the new setting functions is not updated every time for a new vehicle model. Instead, these features allow the user ot conveniently use the connected service when necessary because of an occurence of an error during an update is fundametally prevented. This represents an improvement to the technical area of a connected service which controls a connected vehicle through a portable device.

As claim 1 recites limitations that result in improvement of the relevant technological area, it integrates the alleged judicial exception into a practical application. Thus, claim 1 is not directed to the alleged judicial exception. Claim 10, while different from claim 1, also integrates the alleged judicial exception into a practical application. Thus, claim 10 is also not directed to the alleged judicial exception. Accordingly, claims 1 and 10 recites patent-eligible subject matter. Claims 4-5, 7-9, 13-14, and 16-18 variously depend from claims 1 and 10 and also recite patent eligible subject matter at least due to their dependency from a patent-eligible claim. Claims 2-3, 6, 11-12, and 15 are canceled herewith and, therefore, the rejection of these claims is moot.
Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama

The Office Action rejects claims 1, 4-8, 10, and 13-17 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. 2020/0133261 to Tao et al. ("Tao") in view of U.S. 2014/0025746 to Rhee et al. ("Rhee") and U.S. 2022/0417359 to Tokuyama ("Tokuyama"). Office Action, pp. 4-8.

Applicants respectfully disagree. However, solely in order to advance prosecution, claim 1 is amended to incorporate the subject matter of examined claims 2-3 and 6 and claim 10 is amended to incorporate the subject matter of examined claims 11-12 and 15. The Office Action acknowledges that Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama fail to teach or suggest the subject matter of claims 2-3 and 11-12. Office Action, pp. 9-10. Accordingly, claims 1 and 10 distinguish over Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama, alone or in combination. Claims 4-5, 7-8, 13-14, and 16-17 variously depend from claims 1 and 10 and also distinguish over Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama, alone or in combination, at
least due to this dependency. Claims 6 and 15 are canceled herewith and, therefore, the rejection of these claims is moot.
Claims 1, 5, 10, and 14 further distinguish over Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama on independent grounds, discussed in detail below.

Claim 1 recites, in part, "determine whether to store the user information as a new data set based on the number of times the user information is received in response to determining that the user information is unrecognizable;"

Claim 5 recites, "wherein the server is configured to determine to store the user information as the new data set in response to determining that the number of times the unrecognizable user information is received exceeds the predetermined number of times."

The Office Action acknowledges that these features are not taught or suggested by Tao and Rhee but further alleges that this deficiency is remedied by Tokuyama. Office Action, pp. 5-7. Applicants respectfully disagree with this characterization of the teachings of Tokuyama.
Tokuyama presents an authentication process with reference to FIG. 22A.
" In the process, a face image of a user is used as biometric information.
" In steps S601-S604, an authentication information acquirer 185 causes an imager 11 to

take a photograph of the face of the user operating a mobile terminal 1 and acquires the photograph. If the photograph is blurred, or the user's face cannot be identified from the photograph, the acquirer 185 causes the imager 11 to retake the photograph. When the photograph is not blurred and the users face can be identified from the photograph, the
process moves to step S605. Tokuyama, [0194]-[0195].
" In step S605, an authentication determiner 186 calculates a face authentication value by
comparing feature amount of a face image registered in a biometric information database with a feature amount of the face image acquired by the acquirer 185. When the calculated
face authentication value is equal to or greater than an authentication threshold, the process
moves to step 5606. Tokuyama, [0196].
" In step 5606, determiner 186 further determines whether the calculated face authentication

value is equal to or less than an authentication permission value. If so, the determiner 186 performs an auxiliary authentication that authenticates the user according to the user's habit. For example, the determiner 186 causes the acquirer 185 to acquire a communication connection destination currently connected via a near field communicator 10 and receives the acquired current communication connection destination from the
acquirer 185. Tokuyama, [0197].
" Subsequently, the determiner 186 acquires a user habit database for authentication 182

from a terminal storage 17A. The user habit database for authentication 182 stores information on user-specific habits when operating the mobile terminal and authentication results. User specific habits can include actions when the user operates the mobile terminal 1, a distance between a screen of a display 19 and the user's face, a keystroke, a way of holding the mobile terminal 1, a place where the mobile terminal 1 is used, and a communication environment. A latest state of each user's habit can be a total number of times that a communication connection destination indicated in the acquired information has been connected to so far if the user's habit type is communication
connection. Tokuyama, [0072], [0189], [0198].
" The determiner 186 acquires the acquired information, a number of times, and a pass

condition associated with a communication connection amongst types of user habits stored in the table of user habit database 182. A case in which the pass condition is satisfied is referred to as reliable and a case where the pass condition is not satisfied is referred to as
unreliable. Tokuyama, [0198].

From the forgoing, it can be appreciated that the determination of reliability or unreliability made by Tokuyama is made on the basis of a number of times the communication connection destination indicated in the acquired information has been connected. The communication connection destination has no relation to unrecognizable user information. Similarly, a determination regarding reliability or unreliability in the context of a pass condition also has no relation to unrecognizable user information. Furthermore, the determination of reliability or unreliability in view of a number of times the communication connection destination indicated in
the acquired information has been connected does not result in a further decision whether to store particular data, such as received unrecognizable user data.
Accordingly, one skilled in the are would fail to arrive at "determine whether to store the

user information as a new data set based on the number of times the user information is received in response to determining that the user information is unrecognizable," as recited in examined claim 1 or "wherein the server is configured to determine to store the user information as the new data set in response to determining that the number of times the unrecognizable user information is received exceeds the predetermined number of times," as recited in claim 5.

For at least these reasons, claims 1 and 5 further distinguish over Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama, alone or in any combination. Claims 10 and 15, while different from claims 1 and 5 also distinguish over Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama, alone or in any combination, for at least the same reasons as claims
1 and 5.
Tao, Rhee, Tokuyama, and Corradino

The Office Action rejects claims 2-3, 9, 11-12, and 18 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama in view of U.S. 2011/0215900 to Corradino et al. ("Corradino"). Office Action, pp. 9-11.
Applicants respectfully disagree. However, solely in order to advance prosecution, claim 1 is further amended to incorporate the subject matter of examined claims 2-3 and 6 and recites, in part,
"wherein the user information includes vehicle setting values and attribute
information linked to the vehicle setting values;
wherein the attribute information includes vehicle setting functions and key
IDs respectively matched to the vehicle setting functions; and
wherein the server informs the one or more of the portable device and the
vehicle terminal that the new data set is stored when the user information is stored
as the new data set."
As discussed in detail below, Tao, Rhee, Tokuyama, and Corradino fails to teach or suggest at least these features of claim 1.

Corradino presents systems and methods for management of mobile device communications with reference to FIG. 2, reproduced below. It is assumed that a user of a mobile communication device 110 is within or approaching a vehicle for which the mobile communications management services are configured.
SVG {EMBED HERE} 4.6232.837 2
" In step 202, a mobile communications device 110 detects the presence of a fixed
communications device 126 (e.g., the user of the mobile communications device 110 vehicle
enters the vehicle 120).
" In step 204, an input command is received at the mobile communications device 110 via an
I/O 112 in response to user selections. A logic 115 intercepts this command before execution
and receives biometric data (e.g., fingerprint scan) from a biometric scanner 116.
" At step 206, the logic 115 identifies the user of the mobile communications device , as well

as the user's authorizations (permissions) level. The identification can be implemented by comparing the scanned biometric data with biometric data stored in a memory 108 (e.g., a configuration file 130). The authorization level can be further determined as that listed in the configuration file 130. For example, the configuration file 130 can link attributes such as user name or ID, mobile device number, permissions level, fingerprint scan of the user, vehicle ID,
etc.

The Office Action likens the recited "user information include[ing] vehicle setting values and attribute information linked to the vehicle setting values" and the recited "attribute information include[ing] vehicle setting functions and key IDs respectively matched to the vehicle setting functions" of examined claims 2-3, now incorporated into claim 1, to the configuration file 130 describing linking attributes. Office Action, pp. 9-10. However, the attribute information of Corradino (user name or ID, mobile device number, permissions level, fingerprint scan of the user, vehicle ID) is very different from vehicle setting functions and key IDs matched to such vehicle setting functions. Thus, Corradino's linking of attribute information is very different from user information linking vehicle setting values, vehicle setting functions, and key IDs. Accordingly, Corradino fails to teach or suggest "wherein the user information includes vehicle setting values and attribute information linked to the vehicle setting values" and "wherein the attribute information includes vehicle setting functions and key IDs respectively matched to the vehicle setting functions" as recited in claim 1. Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama are relied upon for other independent claim features and fail to remedy these deficiencies.

For at least these reasons, claim 1 distinguishes over Tao, Rhee, Tokuyama, and Corradino, alone or in any combination. Claim 10, while different from claim 1, also distinguishes over Tao, Rhee, Tokuyama, and Corradino, alone or in any combination for at least the same reasons as claim
1. Accordingly, claims 1 and 10 represent allowable subject matter. Claims 9 and 18 variously depend from claims 1 and 10 and also distinguish over Tao, Rhee, and Tokuyama, alone or in
combination, at least due to this dependency. Claims 2-3 and 11-12 are canceled herewith and, therefore, the rejection of these claims is moot.

In conclusion, Applicants submit that all pending claims are in condition for allowance for at least the reasons discussed above, and allowance thereof is respectfully requested. Applicants' amendment of the claims does not constitute a concession that the claims are not allowable in their unamended form. The Examiner is encouraged to telephone the undersigned Agent for Applicants if such communication is deemed to expedite prosecution of this application.
